# WordPress MCP

Use this skill whenever the user asks Codex to work with WordPress content, SEO, GEO, pages, posts, media, or site abilities through MCP. Also use it when the user asks to open or configure the local WordPress MCP connector dashboard.

## Local Manager

- The local dashboard URL is generated on first start and stored in `data/runtime.json`; do not assume a fixed port.
- To open the dashboard from Codex, run `scripts/open-manager.mjs` from this plugin.
- If `WORDPRESS_MCP_CONNECTOR_ROOT` is set, the opener can start the local connector server before opening the dashboard.
- If the dashboard is not running and no root is configured, start the connector app with `npm start` from the cloned repository.

## Server Routing

- Use the MCP server name generated by the local dashboard for the selected WordPress site.
- If more than one WordPress site exists, operate on one site at a time and state which server is being used.
- If the current workspace clearly belongs to one project, use that matching server unless the user explicitly asks for another site.

## Safety

- Never ask the user to paste WordPress passwords, application passwords, JWTs, bearer tokens, or API headers into chat.
- Prefer drafts, previews, reads, and metadata checks before destructive or irreversible writes.
- Do not delete posts, pages, media, users, plugins, or theme files unless the user explicitly asks for that action in the current turn.
- For SEO or GEO work, preserve existing canonical URLs, slugs, schema fields, and rank-tracking metadata unless the user asks to change them.

## Recommended Workflow

1. List available MCP tools for the chosen server when the exact tool surface is unknown.
2. Read the target post/page/media item before updating it.
3. Make the smallest update that satisfies the request.
4. Report the site, item, and fields changed.
5. If a write cannot be verified through MCP, say so and suggest a WordPress admin check.

## MCP Adapter Call Shape

WordPress MCP Adapter exposes WordPress actions as abilities through wrapper tools.

- Discover abilities with `mcp-adapter-discover-abilities`.
- Inspect an ability with `mcp-adapter-get-ability-info` using `ability_name`.
- Execute an ability with `mcp-adapter-execute-ability` using `ability_name` and `parameters`.

For article draft creation:

```json
{
  "ability_name": "ewpa/create-post",
  "parameters": {
    "title": "Draft title",
    "content": "<p>Draft HTML content</p>",
    "status": "draft"
  }
}
```

Do not call the wrapper with `name`, `ability`, or `input`; those field names are rejected by this adapter.

## Local Uploads

The remote WordPress ability `ewpa/upload-image` imports images from public URLs only. When the user provides a local image path, use the connector-added MCP tool `wordpress-upload-local-image` first.

Example local image upload arguments:

```json
{
  "file_path": "/absolute/path/to/image.jpg",
  "title": "Media title",
  "alt_text": "Descriptive alt text"
}
```

The tool returns `attachment_id` and `url`. Use `attachment_id` as `featured_image_id` for `ewpa/create-post` or `ewpa/update-post`, or insert `url` into the HTML content.

Use `wordpress-upload-local-file` for PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, and other media-library files. It does not install plugin/theme zip packages.

## Expanded Local Tools

The local runner adds extra MCP tools beyond the remote WordPress abilities:

- `wordpress-upload-local-file`: upload PDFs, docs, spreadsheets, zip files, and other media-library files from a local path.
- `wordpress-create-taxonomy-term`: create a term in a REST-exposed taxonomy, including CPT taxonomies. Use this before assigning terms when the term does not exist.
- `wordpress-list-menus`: list REST-exposed WordPress menus and menu locations.
- `wordpress-create-menu-item`: create a navigation menu item when the site's menu REST API is available.
- `wordpress-companion-status`: check whether the optional WordPress MCP Connector Companion plugin is installed.
- `wordpress-create-local-backup`: create a local JSON recovery point for the selected site. Use this before broad edits, cleanup work, SEO migrations, plugin/theme changes, or any operation that could be hard to undo.
- `wordpress-update-llms-text`: update `/llms.txt` or `/llms-full.txt`; requires the companion plugin.
- `wordpress-purge-litespeed-cache`: purge LiteSpeed Cache; requires the companion plugin and the site's `LiteSpeed 清缓存` permission switch enabled in the local dashboard.
- `wordpress-install-local-package`: install a local plugin/theme `.zip`; requires the companion plugin and the site's package-install permission switch enabled in the local dashboard.

Package installs are high risk and disabled by default. Do not use `wordpress-install-local-package` unless the user explicitly asks to install a trusted package and confirms the dashboard permission switch is enabled for that site.

Backup strategies are configured per site in the local dashboard. The runner may create a pre-change recovery point automatically before write or delete tools when the site's strategy enables it. If a pre-change backup fails, do not continue with the write until the user explicitly accepts the risk or fixes backup access.

If enabling package install or llms.txt permissions fails with a companion sync warning, explain that the feature requires the WordPress-side companion plugin to be installed and active in wp-admin. Download location: https://github.com/baixinyao2011-beep/wordpress-mcp-connector/tree/main/wordpress-plugin/wordpress-mcp-connector-companion
